name: Lychee
water: Regular deep watering; consistent moisture while fruit develops
climate: Warm subtropical to tropical; protect young trees from frost
tip: Shelter from strong wind and avoid damaging shallow roots.

name: Longan
tip: A slightly drier, cooler period can help flowering on established trees.

name: Rambutan
water: High, consistent moisture with excellent drainage
tip: Protect from drying winds and maintain a thick organic mulch.

name: Custard Apple
water: Regular during flowering and fruit development
climate: Subtropical to tropical; warm frost-free sites
tip: Hand pollination can improve fruit set where natural pollination is poor.

name: Dragon Fruit
climate: Warm subtropical to tropical; frost sensitive
tip: Train stems up a strong post with a top frame for hanging branches.

name: Star Fruit
tip: Protect young trees from wind and frost.

name: Tamarillo
depth: Seed 5 mm; transplants at nursery level
climate: Cool subtropical to mild temperate; frost sensitive
tip: Shelter brittle branches from strong winds and mulch the shallow roots.

name: Jaboticaba
climate: Subtropical to tropical; established trees tolerate mild cool conditions
tip: Consistent water during flowering and fruiting encourages better crops.

name: Sapodilla
water: Regular while establishing; moderate once mature
tip: Harvest fruit mature but firm and allow it to soften off the tree.

name: Jackfruit
depth: Seed 2–3 cm; trees at nursery level
climate: Tropical to warm subtropical; frost sensitive
tip: Allow substantial room—the mature tree and fruit can become very large.

name: Coconut
tip: Plant only where long-term warmth is reliable and allow overhead clearance.

name: Date Palm
water: Deep watering; reduce humidity around ripening fruit
climate: Hot arid to semi-arid; dry summers best for fruit
tip: Male and female palms are separate; fruit production requires pollination.

name: Olive
climate: Mediterranean, temperate and suitable dry regions
tip: Avoid waterlogged soil and choose cultivars suited to local winter chill.

name: Pecan
water: Regular deep watering during nut development
climate: Temperate to subtropical with warm summers
tip: Plant compatible cultivars nearby to improve cross-pollination.

name: Walnut
water: Deep regular watering during dry periods
climate: Cool to temperate with adequate winter chill
tip: Give the large tree plenty of space away from vegetable beds and structures.

name: Almond
water: Regular during establishment and kernel development
climate: Temperate/Mediterranean; cool winters and dry ripening weather
tip: Late frost can damage blossom; choose a cultivar appropriate to local frost timing.

name: Hazelnut
tip: Grow compatible cultivars together because cross-pollination is usually required.

name: Chestnut
water: Regular while establishing and during dry periods
climate: Cool to temperate with winter chill
tip: Plant more than one compatible cultivar for reliable nut set.

name: Pistachio
water: Deep watering; drought tolerant once established
climate: Hot dry summers and cool winters
tip: Male and female trees are separate; include a suitable male pollinator.

name: Cashew
depth: Seed 2–3 cm; trees at nursery level
tip: The raw shell contains irritating compounds; nuts require proper processing before eating.

name: Pawpaw
tip: Plant genetically different trees or compatible cultivars to improve pollination.

name: Kumquat
water: Regular deep watering; allow surface soil to dry slightly
tip: Mulch widely but keep mulch clear of the trunk.

name: Pomelo
tip: Warm conditions produce the best fruit quality; protect young trees from frost.

name: Tangelo
tip: Some cultivars crop better with another compatible citrus nearby for pollination.

name: Blood Orange
climate: Temperate to subtropical; cool nights can enhance flesh colour
tip: Feed citrus through the growing season and keep grass away from the root zone.

name: Yuzu
climate: Cool temperate to subtropical; relatively cold-tolerant citrus
tip: Wear gloves when pruning because many yuzu trees carry strong thorns.

name: Buddha's Hand
climate: Warm temperate to subtropical; protect from severe frost
tip: Excellent drainage is important; avoid persistently wet roots.

name: Black Sapote
tip: Fruit is ready when fully mature and allowed to soften before eating.

name: White Sapote
tip: Prune to control size because mature trees can become large.

name: Miracle Fruit
climate: Humid tropical to warm subtropical; frost sensitive
tip: Requires acidic soil; avoid alkaline water and lime-rich soil.

name: Acerola
depth: Seed 5–10 mm; plants at nursery level
tip: Prune lightly after harvest to maintain a manageable productive canopy.

name: Surinam Cherry
climate: Subtropical to tropical; tolerates mild cool conditions
tip: Fruit flavour varies greatly between seedlings; named cultivars are more predictable.

name: Prickly Pear
depth: Bury lower 5–8 cm of cured pad
water: Low; allow soil to dry between watering
tip: Use only permitted non-invasive varieties and handle pads and fruit carefully due to spines/glochids.

name: Cape Gooseberry
tip: Provide support as branches become heavy with fruit.

name: Pepino
depth: Cuttings planted 5–8 cm deep; seed 5 mm
tip: Support sprawling plants and protect ripening fruit from pests.

name: Elderberry
tip: Cook ripe berries before culinary use and do not eat leaves, stems or unripe fruit.

name: Cranberry
tip: Grow in strongly acidic soil; ordinary alkaline garden beds perform poorly.

name: Loganberry
tip: Train canes along wires and remove old fruiting canes after harvest.

name: Youngberry
tip: Trellis long canes for easier picking and airflow.

name: Jujube
climate: Temperate to hot dry regions; winter dormant
tip: Choose a named cultivar and remove unwanted root suckers.

name: Rose
depth: Graft union just above soil in mild climates
climate: Most Australian temperate/subtropical gardens with cultivar selection
tip: Good airflow and morning sun help reduce fungal disease.

name: Petunia
water: Regular; allow slight drying between watering
tip: Trim leggy stems and deadhead to encourage repeat flowering.

name: Snapdragon
tip: Pinch young plants for bushier growth; taller varieties may need support.

name: Alyssum
climate: Temperate to subtropical; often cool-season in hot areas
tip: Shear lightly after a flush of flowers to encourage reblooming.

name: Cornflower
tip: Direct sow because seedlings dislike excessive root disturbance.

name: Foxglove
harvest: Often flowers in second season; some cultivars first year
sun: Part shade to sun in cool climates
tip: All parts are toxic if eaten; site away from children and grazing animals.

name: Hollyhock
harvest: Flowers 4–6 months or second season depending on type
tip: Provide airflow and avoid wetting foliage to reduce rust problems.

name: Geranium
harvest: Flowers within months from established plants
climate: Temperate to subtropical depending on species
tip: Avoid constantly wet soil and remove spent flowers.

name: Pelargonium
climate: Temperate to subtropical; protect from hard frost
tip: Excellent drainage prevents stem and root rot.

name: Begonia
propagation: Seed, leaf/stem cuttings or tubers depending on type
depth: Surface sow seed; tubers shallow with top near surface
harvest: Flowers about 12–20 weeks depending on type
climate: Temperate to tropical depending on species
tip: Protect foliage from harsh afternoon sun and keep good airflow.
